scientific_hypothesis: A dual-cavity Fabry-Perot structure using Si/SiO2 Bragg pairs can achieve comparable dual-band transmission to ZnS/MgF2 while potentially reducing absorption in the 4.45-5.00 μm suppression band.
expected_advantages: Si has lower mid-IR absorption than ZnS beyond 4 μm
SiO2 is low-loss across entire 2.5-5 μm range
known_risks: Si absorption may still be significant at 4.5+ μm
Si/SiO2 stress mismatch on CaF2 substrate
Higher index contrast may create stronger sidelobes in suppression bands
expected_observations: best_target_score should rise with pair count if Si absorption is low enough in suppression bands
tightest_margin should be comparable to route_01 if material choice is not the limiting factor
If Si absorption dominates, best_target_score will plateau with suppression band transmittance remaining elevated
valid_candidates should remain stable if 22-layer Si/SiO2 stack is physically viable on Daimon-20
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if tightest_margin becomes negative for three consecutive rounds, material absorption is likely limiting, stop and compare to route_01 results
